metadata.description: Governance as a by-product of doing the work: a harness-agnostic set of assistant configurations for academic data science. 6 workflow-plane planner plugins (project, govern, curate, analyze, process, disseminate) run DataLad natively, as they would git, and delegate other tools to capability-plane doers (nipoppy, bids, containers, archive, annotate, compendium, liab) and their CLI toolboxes, so every computation and every administrative change runs through one DataLad provenance chain, recorded in the commit history and every research object is Self-contained, Tracked, Actionable, Modular, Portable, Ephemeral and Distributable (see docs/stamped.md). The default export is a living compendium — provenanced dataset, re-executable article, agent-callable method bundle, self-hostable deployment — cross-linked by DOI. Status: both planes are built and every capability has a toolbox; what has not happened is execution — most paths are gated, the gates are tested, and the tools behind them have not been run. The evaluation protocol is specified and unrun (see docs/motivation.md).

plugins.name: project
plugins.description: Project lifecycle planner: scaffold a new YODA/BIDS DataLad study and orient a researcher (coordinator agent) on where a project stands.

plugins.name: govern
plugins.description: Governance planner (Manage & Comply lane): init-ledger gives an existing dataset a project.yaml (the brownfield entry point, refusing to overwrite one); dmp turns a Data Management Plan's promises into tracked obligations; ethics-track records IRB/IACUC protocols, expiries and amendments and flags renewals; preregister freezes a comparison's spec before execution; obligations tracks and resolves outstanding commitments; qc-review and stamped-assess report conformance and STAMPED coverage per dimension, scoring what they could not check as unassessed rather than zero.

plugins.name: analyze
plugins.description: Analysis planner: plan-analysis recommends a statistical approach and lists the assumptions it rests on as unchecked, reporting no statistic of its own; propose-comparison opens each comparison on its own branch; scaffold-analysis emits a provenance-wrapped script stub whose placeholder raises rather than returning a plausible number; run-comparison executes it with full (optionally containerized) provenance; plot draws figures only from produced outputs; gen-report assembles results, QC and provenance with a required gaps section; checkpoint takes clean snapshots and manage-product groups kept comparisons into deliverables.

plugins.name: curate
plugins.description: Curation planner: raw-to-bids converts raw acquisitions to a BIDS layout via nipoppy with DataLad provenance; annotate and gen-data-dict enrich a dataset's metadata (dataset_description.json, participants.json data dictionary, BIDS sidecars, controlled-term mappings); merge-data joins external tabular sources on a declared key and reports what did not match rather than dropping it; deidentify makes identifier removal a provenanced run with a recorded approach and a required residual-risk statement, and refuses to present that record as a compliance determination. Advances STAMPED Self-containment + Actionability.

plugins.name: process
plugins.description: Processing planner: run nipoppy pipelines (fMRIPrep, MRIQC, ...) on BIDS data with full DataLad provenance, then record completion. Runs DataLad directly and delegates nipoppy mechanics to the nipoppy doer.

plugins.name: disseminate
plugins.description: Dissemination planner: turn provenanced work into published, linked products. publish pushes committed state to a sibling and verifies an independent clone can retrieve the outputs; dataset-release cuts a citable versioned release with a DOI via the archive doer; link-outputs cross-links products; draft-manuscript and reporting-checklist produce the paper; executable-article (NeuroLibre), agent-bundle (Paper2Agent) and liab-deploy (Lab-in-a-Box) produce the living compendium. submission-track records where a product was submitted and what came back as an append-only submissions[] history, so a resubmission does not erase the first venue's outcome and no decision is recorded before it arrives. Advances STAMPED Distributability.

plugins.name: nipoppy
plugins.description: Nipoppy doer: the tool subagent that constructs/validates nipoppy pipeline commands and hands dataset-mutating steps back to the planner to run under `datalad run`.

plugins.name: containers
plugins.description: Containers doer: authors and builds a project's compute environments along the path people actually use — Dockerfile → OCI image → .sif — and expects several per project (an authored analysis environment beside vendored pipeline images, and derived images that add the project's own tools to a standard base), each named and each pinned for its kind. Registration and running stay with the planner, which runs `datalad containers-add` and `containers-run` itself.

plugins.name: containers-cli
plugins.description: Containers skill toolbox, split by job rather than by binary: dockerfile translates a declared environment into a Dockerfile and refuses when what it declares would not rebuild, oci-build builds it with Podman or Docker and says which ran and whether it was rootless, apptainer converts the result to the .sif a cluster runs. Two pins it will not waive: an unpinned manifest and a mutable image tag both yield containers that run and do not rebuild.

plugins.name: bids
plugins.description: BIDS doer: read-only validation of a dataset against the Brain Imaging Data Structure (bids-validator + structural checks); reports conformance, never modifies the dataset.

plugins.name: archive
plugins.description: Archive doer: deposits a released version to an external archive (OSF/Zenodo/DataCite) and mints a persistent DOI; reports 'unminted' rather than fabricating one when credentials are absent.

plugins.name: annotate
plugins.description: Annotate doer: builds and validates a dataset's machine-readable metadata — participants.json data dictionaries and controlled-term coverage against Neurobagel/SNOMED, ReproSchema and NIDM; reports a term it could not look up as 'unannotated' rather than recalling one, and an uninstalled backend as unavailable rather than as zero matches.

plugins.name: compendium
plugins.description: Compendium doer: scaffolds and builds living research products — MyST and Jupyter Book projects, repo2data fetches, and Paper2Agent-style agent bundles — wiring each figure to the provenanced run that produced it and building inside the project's pinned container. Reports an untraceable figure as 'unprovenanced' rather than embedding it, a partial build as partial, and refuses to build on the host and call it pinned.

plugins.name: liab
plugins.description: Lab-in-a-Box doer: plans self-hosted research infrastructure, applies it only on an explicit confirmation that names the target host, and proves the dataset is retrievable with a datalad get. The only doer whose mistakes are not confined to a working tree, so it plans by default, reports a partial application as partial, never retries a failed apply, and never calls a deployment 'working' on the strength of a green pyinfra run.

plugins.name: datalad-cli
plugins.description: DataLad toolbox for running DataLad natively, the way the assistant runs git. It has one `datalad` skill that routes by verb to 19 verb references (create, run, save, containers-run, siblings, push, ...). It also ships always-loaded rules, hooks that guard `git commit` and `git push`, and `dsh-log`, which reads harness activity back from `DSH-*` commit lines.

plugins.name: nipoppy-cli
plugins.description: Nipoppy skill toolbox, split by command class rather than by verb: nipoppy-query reads state, nipoppy-track refreshes the derived status files, nipoppy-compute constructs the commands that produce data and refuses to execute them, and nipoppy-setup scaffolds a dataset and its pipeline configurations. The split is the safety property — nipoppy records nothing about how derivatives came to be, so a computation executed bare produces a tree nothing can re-derive. Advances STAMPED Tracking and Actionability.

plugins.name: archive-cli
plugins.description: Archive skill toolbox: one skill per backend (OSF, Zenodo, DataCite) for deposit, DOI minting and related identifiers, plus the offline readiness check the archive doer runs before any deposit.

plugins.name: bids-cli
plugins.description: BIDS skill toolbox: bids-validator as a first-class, user-invocable skill, plus the offline check the bids doer runs first. Two different programs are called 'the BIDS validator' and they take different flags, so the skill confirms the installed surface instead of assuming it, and reports 'unverified' rather than a pass when none is installed.

plugins.name: liab-cli
plugins.description: Lab-in-a-Box skill toolbox: pyinfra deployment planning and, on an explicit target-naming instruction, application; forgejo repository creation on an instance that already runs — plus the offline check the liab doer runs first. Plan-by-default is a constraint rather than a preference, because the blast radius is a machine rather than a working tree, and forgejo refuses to guess a repository's visibility because neither answer is undoable. Advances STAMPED Distributability.

plugins.name: compendium-cli
plugins.description: Compendium skill toolbox: MyST project scaffolding and building, Jupyter Book builds that report what was executed rather than only what rendered, repo2data fetches constructed as recorded runs, and MCP bundle scaffolding checked against the harness's own lint — plus the offline check the compendium doer runs first. Each is explicit about what a green result does not prove: building a document is not making it reproducible, a MyST build exits 0 with unresolved references so a clean build is never reported without its warnings, a fetch is not provenance, and a bundle emitted in the harness format is a claim until the lint has run over it.

plugins.name: annotate-cli
plugins.description: Annotate skill toolbox: one skill per annotation tool (bagel-cli for Neurobagel, pynidm for NIDM, reproschema for instrument schemas, snomed-lookup for clinical codes), plus the offline per-backend check the annotate doer runs first. Most of them validate terms rather than find them, and each says so.
